verdicts.quote: when the whole file passes every check, every row becomes a user, and the store changes in one step: afterwards either all rows exist or none do.
each error with its row number and a message mapped from its code
A row repeating a normalized email already present on an earlier row […] → `duplicate_in_file` carrying `first_row`; a row whose normalized email belongs to an existing user → `email_taken`.
The import never grants administrator rights […] F-UNKNOWNCOL (`role` column set to `admin`) → 422 `unknown_column`; no user is created and none is an administrator.
the import API accepts a request only from an authenticated principal the product currently treats as an administrator.
verdicts.missing: The admin role is required. The specification does not distinguish bulk-import authority from the permission to create one user within that role.

verdicts.quote: The header is the first non-blank record; header names are trimmed and compared case-insensitively. Required columns are `email` and `name`; their order is free. […] header (missing, unknown, duplicate columns are all reported together)
UTF-8 (a leading byte-order mark is ignored), comma-delimited […] a quoted field may contain commas and line breaks), records separated by LF or CRLF.
a failure mid-way leaves the store as before […] The import never grants administrator rights, sets a password, or sends an email or invitation.
content of 524,289 bytes or more → 413 `file_too_large`; 1,001 or more data rows → 422 `too_many_rows` […] Neither creates a user or validates rows.
F-A-UPPERHDR → 201 created 1 […] F-EMPTY and F-BLANKS → 422 `empty_file`; F-HEADERONLY → 422 `no_data_rows`
re-posting F-A after AC-6.1 changes nothing: 422 `email_taken` for rows 2, 3 and 4, count stays 6 (a retry never duplicates).
The response is returned only after the outcome is durable. No queue, worker, job record or status endpoint.
verdicts.missing: The response tells the admin when an accepted file finishes. Larger files must be split, and the specification provides no background processing or later completion notice for them.

verdicts.quote: The import never grants administrator rights, sets a password, or sends an email or invitation.
a created user has the same role, status and credential state as a user created through the product's existing single-user admin path
verdicts.missing: The single-user defaults are unknown, so active versus pending status and the usual first sign-in method are unspecified. Account recovery is prescribed only for the fallback where no single-user admin path exists.

verdicts.quote: the import request, memory | that request only […] freed at request end, never written (R-10) […] no endpoint returns a past import's file, rows or report

acting admin's id, `outcome` (`created`, `rejected`, `failed`), data-row count when determinable, `created` count […] an operator can answer who imported, when, and what happened, without seeing personal data.
the admin can fix the file and choose it again. […] cancelling an in-flight import (cancelling the page request would not undo a server effect)
verdicts.missing: Cancellation is explicitly excluded. The recovery flow resubmits the corrected file. No behavior is specified for selecting and retrying just the reported rows after an atomic rejection.

verdicts.quote: the numeric time limit of the deployed runtime is not known here. […] shows a busy indicator with no invented progress figure
verdicts.missing: The maximum completion time still needs a value. The busy indicator shows that work is underway without showing how much has finished.

verdicts.quote: preserves, by reference, whatever the existing single-user creation does […] Existing users are never changed (PD-5).
